ideas.title: Buy the dollar washout that runs into the payroll print

legs.contract: DXU6 - ICE US Dollar Index future, Sep 2026, $1,000 per index point, min tick 0.005 = $5

exit.event_anchor: hold spans the 2026-08-07 payroll release; exit at the 2026-08-10 close

ideas.thesis: The dollar has fallen for a week, with its 5-day return in the bottom 6% of the trailing year, while the 3-month uptrend is untouched at the 88th percentile. The tape is reading that as the start of a dollar downtrend. The evidence says a washout inside an intact uptrend reverses when a payroll print sits in the window, and that the print is the reason: the pullback cell on its own is dead at episode t of 1.04 to 1.23, and the plain day-before-payroll cell is dead at N=318, t=-0.24. Only the intersection pays, and it has paid in 79% of 43 windows. On the other side are momentum FX programs that sell a five-day dollar decline without looking at the calendar, plus the month-end flow that mechanically concentrates dollar selling into the first days of a month and then stops.

evidence.summary: Trigger: DX 5-day return rank <= 25 and 63-day rank >= 70 and a payroll print inside the next 3 sessions. Executable basis (buy MOO at the entry session, exit MOC three sessions later): N=43 signal days, +0.529%, t=4.50, 79.1% up; 29 declustered episodes +0.482%, t=2.98. Today's exact geometry, print two sessions after the signal close: N=14, +0.620%, t=2.74, 78.6% up, worst -0.83%. Median worst excursion inside the hold -0.25%, 5th percentile -0.97%. Two disclosures: 87% of historical signals sit in a turn-of-month window, and within turn-of-month days alone the payroll split still roughly doubles the edge (+0.575% vs +0.255%), so the honest claim is a dollar washout into the turn of the month with payrolls as the named catalyst; and about 43% of the payoff is the print day itself, so part of this is a coin flip on a release.
evidence.control: Unconditional identical MOO-to-MOC 3-session hold on every session: +0.011%. Both single legs are dead on their own: pullback with no print in the window N=271, t=0.14; print in the window with no pullback N=703, t=-1.05. Placebo events (every payroll shifted 5, 7 or 11 sessions) all die or go negative.
evidence.era_note: Both halves positive and significant: pre-2018 N=30, +0.536%, t=3.43; 2018 onward N=13, +0.512%, t=3.34, 84.6% up. Weakest sub-era is 2013-2018 at episode t around 0.74. The trigger's parameter neighbourhood is not a knife edge: all 23 cells of the rank5 x rank63 grid are positive, t from 1.89 to 4.83.

ideas.survived: The move to the executable entry. Eleven candidates died today because their edge lived in the overnight gap between the signal close and the next open; here the close-basis +0.528% becomes +0.529% on a market-on-open entry, a give-up of half a basis point. The cost check also passes rather than being waved through: one round trip in DX futures is about 1.5 bps against a 48 to 53 bps episode edge.
ideas.what_kills_it: A payroll print soft enough to put rate cuts back on the table. Watch the dollar in the hour after 8:30 on Friday: if DX is still below Thursday's close at Friday's cash close, the impulse this cell measures has not fired and the remaining session will not repair it. Separately, a dollar close deep enough to drop the 63-day return rank under 70 voids the setup outright, because the uptrend leg is load-bearing.
ideas.overlap: Nothing in the systematic book trades FX, and the trend sleeve's 12-ETF universe deliberately excludes UUP, so there is no direct conflict. The event sleeve holds nothing until the 2026-08-21 opex. Real overlap is with today's short-TLT idea: both are the same dollar-up, rates-up impulse over the same three sessions, so treat them as roughly one macro bet and halve them if you take both. One more honest headwind: this state has occurred 15 times inside a pre-CPI window, as today's does, and averaged -0.306% (t=-1.42) over the same hold. Small, post-hoc, not a kill, but it is the weak side of the sample.

ideas.title: Buy the index the week hedges get thrown away

exit.event_anchor: exit at the 2026-08-10 close, before the 2026-08-12 CPI print

ideas.thesis: The daily CBOE equity put/call closed at the 7.7th percentile of its trailing year after a week in which the index rose 5.5% to a new high. Today's own seasonal board reads that as complacency and files it under contrarian-short context. Nineteen years of the series say the opposite over the next three sessions: bottom-decile daily readings have been followed by a small positive drift with a 61% hit rate, and the effect survives declustering at two different gaps. Who is on the other side: everyone treating a low put/call as a mechanical sell signal, and the hedgers who have already lifted protection and are therefore no longer a source of forced selling into a dip. The edge is 18 basis points over three days, so this is a small, high-frequency drift trade and should be sized like one, not like a view.

evidence.summary: Trigger: daily CBOE equity put/call at or below the 10th percentile of its trailing 252 days, lagged one business day exactly as the live feed arrives (today's aligned reading is 7.7, dated 2026-08-04). Buy MOO, exit MOC three sessions later. N=553 signal days, +0.203%, t=3.49, 61.3% up; 174 declustered episodes at gap 10, +0.262%, t=2.42; 114 episodes at gap 21, +0.303%, t=2.30. Leave-one-year-out floor t=1.86 (dropping 2009). Worst window -6.80%. Today carries two extra conditions the base cell does not require: the 10-day average of the ratio is still at the 71st percentile (a fast flip from fear to complacency) and SPY's 5-day return is at the 100th percentile. That three-way slice is N=15, +0.683%, t=1.16 at this horizon: same sign, larger mean, no significance. Treat the base cell as the claim and today's slice as neither confirmation nor contradiction.
evidence.control: Unconditional identical MOO-to-MOC 3-session hold on every session: +0.087%. The measured lift is +0.175 percentage points with a Welch t of 1.58 against that drift, which is the honest size of the effect. The low-put/call-with-a-cool-tape control (N=470) behaves the same way, so today's hot tape is not required for the result and is not contradicted by it.
evidence.era_note: Both eras positive, the recent one weaker: pre-2018 N=270, +0.266%, t=3.35; 2018 onward N=283, +0.143%, t=1.69. The series only begins in 2006-11, so there is no genuinely out-of-sample era to appeal to. The 5- and 10-session versions are also positive (episode t 2.46 and 3.09) but their lift over drift is no larger, which is why the horizon is three.

ideas.survived: Declustering, which killed eleven of today's nineteen candidates. A signal-day t of 3.49 on overlapping windows is exactly the shape that collapsed elsewhere this morning; here the episode t is still 2.42 at gap 10 and 2.30 at gap 21, and the leave-one-year-out floor is 1.86. The sibling idea it came from did not survive: conditioning on the fear-to-complacency flip adds nothing over the plain bottom-decile reading and flips sign on a one-day lag shift, so that framing was dropped rather than pitched.
ideas.what_kills_it: The put/call snapping back while the index stalls. Concretely: if Friday's payroll print takes the index down more than 1% and the equity put/call closes back above its 10-day average, the positioning premise has gone and the position should be cut at Friday's close rather than carried into Monday. A three-day drift trade has no room to sit through a regime change.
ideas.overlap: Direct and large, and it cuts against the book. The fragility dial's 10-day average of the 63-day column is 54.7 and the P/C fear state is OFF, which under the bands shipped yesterday zeroes all six frag_risk_bands carriers, so the systematic dip-buy family is switched off this morning and the exposure leg is at 0.0x. This is a manual index long placed on the exact morning the book's own machinery has stepped back. That is a deliberate disagreement about a three-day horizon rather than a regime call, and it is sized at 20 bps for that reason.

ideas.title: Sell duration on the same dollar impulse

exit.event_anchor: hold spans the 2026-08-07 payroll release; cover at the 2026-08-10 close

ideas.thesis: The dollar setup that carries today's DX trade has a bond leg nobody in this repo has measured. On the 43 occasions the dollar washed out inside an intact 3-month uptrend with a payroll print in the window, long-duration Treasuries fell over the same three sessions in 72.5% of them, averaging -0.54%. The variant perception is about which asset carries the impulse: the bond market prices payrolls as a two-sided event, while this cell says the dollar's mean reversion and the duration selloff are one move and the bond leg is the cleaner statistical object of the two on lift over its own drift. On the other side are duration buyers who have been adding into a soft-data narrative that a week of dollar weakness encouraged, and the month-end index extension buying that unwinds in the first sessions of a month. TLT is already below its 200-day average with the 10-year at a 75th-percentile 63-day rank, so the trade leans with the trend rather than against it.

evidence.summary: Same trigger as the dollar idea: DX 5-day return rank <= 25 and 63-day rank >= 70 and a payroll print inside the next 3 sessions. Short TLT MOO at the entry session, cover MOC three sessions later. N=40 signal days, -0.536%, t=-3.21, only 27.5% of windows up (so the short won 72.5%); 27 declustered episodes at gap 10, -0.615%, t=-2.88; 24 episodes at gap 21, -0.552%, t=-2.34. Worst window for the short -2.56%. Six dollar-sensitive assets were swept on this one trigger (GLD, SLV, GDX, EEM, TLT, XLE) and only TLT cleared; that sweep is disclosed, not hidden, and its multiplicity is tested below.
evidence.control: Unconditional identical MOO-to-MOC 3-session hold in TLT: +0.049%. The lift is -0.585 percentage points with a Welch t of -3.48 on signal days and -3.10 on episodes. Multiplicity: a permutation null over the same six-asset grid, redrawing the signal dates 2000 times, gives a median largest Welch t of 1.50 and a 95th percentile of 2.67, so P(a coin-flip grid produces the observed 3.10) = 0.015.
evidence.era_note: This is the weakness, and it caps the grade. The effect is pre-2018: 18 episodes before 2018 average -0.878% at t=-3.88, while the 9 episodes from 2018 onward average -0.089% at t=-0.21. The modern era does not confirm it. Nine observations cannot refute it either, but a single era is what this is, and the second failed week should retire it.

ideas.survived: The multiplicity test. Measuring six dollar-sensitive assets on one trigger is precisely the sweep shape that got the whole cross-asset payroll family killed earlier this morning, when its best cell of 36 was beaten by a coin-flip grid a quarter of the time. Here the permutation null on the six-cell grid's largest Welch t puts the observed 3.10 at p = 0.015, so the winner of this sweep is not what randomness produces. The gold, silver, miner, EM and energy legs of the same sweep were all insignificant and are reported alongside it.
ideas.what_kills_it: A soft payroll print that revives the cut trade. If the 10-year yield closes Friday below Thursday's close, the impulse this cell measures has not fired and the short should be covered into Friday's close rather than carried to Monday. Given that the 2018-onward sample is flat, one clean failure is enough to say the cell is gone rather than unlucky.
ideas.overlap: Same macro impulse as today's long-dollar idea over the identical three sessions, so the two are close to one bet: if you take both, halve them, or take the DX leg alone since it is the stronger cell and both eras confirm it. No systematic strategy holds Treasuries directly. The trend sleeve's universe includes TLT but its state is flat and it only rebalances at month end, so there is no live conflict this week. Borrow on TLT is general collateral and the fund's monthly distribution goes ex at the start of the month, which this hold has already cleared.

killed.title: Long XLU / short SPY on the defensive washout
killed.reason: The pitched trigger did not fire (its z10 leg passed by 2.8e-5). On the only form that fires, episode t never clears 1.4 at any horizon, XLU beats its own drift inside the cell so the short leg is a measured drag, plain long SPY doubles the pair's return at identical vol, and today sits in the rising-rate subset where the episode edge is +0.05% to +0.14%.

killed.title: Short USO / long XLE on the crude dislocation
killed.reason: 92% of the edge is the XLE long; the USO short is t=+0.24 with a 40% hit rate. The -7pp relative trigger actually lowers episode t versus the crude washout alone, 2020 is +176R of the total, and 2021-2026 is outright negative at a 20% hit rate. Today's configuration (USO 13.8% above its 200d) is the flat-to-negative subset.

killed.title: August and midterm payroll cross-asset fingerprint
killed.reason: 132 looks across 6 assets, 2 windows and 3 conditionings. Best cell |t|=3.14, which a coin-flip grid of the same shape beats 25% of the time. Only VIX moves on the print day and post-payroll vol is already in the registry as swept and empty. Today's conditioning collapses N to 1.

killed.title: SMH violent bounce inside a drawdown
killed.reason: The cell is a fade, not a continuation, and the fade is entirely 2000-2009. The 2018-onward 5-session episode mean is exactly 0.000%. Today's window straddles the AMAT print, and the 2018+ with-a-semis-print bucket is +0.38% at t=0.63, the wrong sign for the fade.

killed.title: Fragility-dial velocity into a new high
killed.reason: One four-day episode (the February 2020 top) carries the entire effect; dropping it flips every horizon positive. A 7-point threshold wobble, which is the documented recompute-vintage drift, flips the sign and halves N. HAC regression puts all significance on dial level, not velocity, and level is already a known-dead surface.

killed.title: Nearest-neighbour analogue to today's tape
killed.reason: The 25 nearest neighbours lift forward 5-session returns by +0.02pp over baseline and the 10-session lift is negative. The sign flips between k=5 (t=-3.55) and k=15 (t=+1.28) and converges on the baseline by k=100. Dropping one arbitrary feature moves the 10-session number from +0.19 to +1.14. Today's tape has no informative analogue.

killed.title: Long AAPL / short QQQ on the mega-cap laggard
killed.reason: The strict cell has exactly one historical instance (2018-01-26) and it lost 2.72% over five sessions. Broadening it produces a t of 3.49 that is entirely pre-2018; at today's -16.4pp gap magnitude the eight modern instances average -3.5% at three sessions. The bigger-N version is alive only in a dead era and the modern evidence points the other way.

killed.title: Long SLV / short GLD on the silver catch-up
killed.reason: The market-on-open entry cuts the 3-session t from 2.09 to 1.58 and the 5-session t from 0.94 to 0.25; 10 sessions is negative. Declustered it is N=36 at t=1.31. Pre-2016, which is most of the sample, is flat to negative at every horizon.

killed.title: Long XLE alone after a crude washout
killed.reason: The handed-over headline did not reproduce (+1.46% not +3.32%). Episode t is 1.35-1.40 and falls below the buy-and-hold baseline at gap 21. The excess over SPY has a negative median and a leave-one-year-out floor of -0.05, so it is a 1.11-beta energy long. Today's window contains payrolls, CPI and PPI, and the CPI-in-window cohort averages +0.03% at t=0.05.

killed.title: Gold thrust out of a downtrend
killed.reason: Eleven usable observations across seven years, no t above 1.53. The pre-registered threshold grid fails: at 1.5 and 1.75 ATR the below-200d filter is negative while the above-200d subset carries the signal, so the trend filter is anti-predictive. No historical event carried both a payroll and a CPI print in its window, as today's would, and the two payroll-window events both lost.

killed.title: Long SVXY on VIX term-structure carry at index highs
killed.reason: Not unproven, sign-negative. The trigger selects 25% of the tape and underperforms SVXY's own drift at every horizon; in the -0.5x era that actually exists it averages -0.25% over five sessions against a +0.28% baseline, with all 15 threshold-grid cells negative. The trigger was continuously ON through 22-26 January 2018, ten sessions before the -1x product lost 90%.

killed.title: Long EEM on a violent surge off a dead base
killed.reason: The dead-base leg is destructive, not decorative: it moves the surge cell from +0.16% to -0.56% at five sessions. N=18 days over 23 years, excess versus SPY -0.48% at a 31% hit rate, 14 of 16 observations pre-2012, and EFA and FXI do not confirm. Today would be a day-2 entry, and day-2 entries run -1.62% at t=-2.04.

killed.title: Tech-over-defensive five-day blowout
killed.reason: The percentile form has no sign at all on episodes; the fixed +10pp form points at reversal but 34 of its 44 days are the 2000-2002 unwind and dropping 2000 flips it. The pair carries a +1.79 net beta to SPY, so it is a levered index long labelled relative value, and hedged it is negative at all three horizons.

killed.title: Put/call complacency flip from fear to greed
killed.reason: The interaction is empty and backwards: requiring the 10-day average to stay elevated makes the cell weaker than the plain bottom-decile reading at 5 and 10 sessions. A one-business-day lag shift moves the 3-session t from -0.15 to +1.31, which is noise pretending to be a signal.

killed.title: Macro-print density into an index high
killed.reason: Signal-day t of 0.04 to 0.82 before any attack. The cell's trading-day-of-month distribution is concentrated on days 2-5, and against a day-of-month-matched control the density adds -0.22 to +0.29 in t. The whole apparent lift lives in 6 observations whose payroll geometry is the opposite of today's.

killed.title: Pre-CPI drift in equities, bonds, gold and the dollar
killed.reason: 24 pre-specified cells, best |t| = 2.44, which a random event calendar beats 47% of the time. The one cell with a pulse is a knife edge on the entry offset (t of 0.96, 2.44, 1.25 at 3, 4 and 5 sessions), loses 40% to a day-of-month-matched control, and its payroll-contaminated subset, which is today's, carries a third of the edge with no significance.

killed.title: Long XLU outright after a relative washout
killed.reason: The t of 3.13 that motivated it is overlapping-window inflation. Declustered on the executable entry the lift over XLU's own drift is +0.097% at 21 sessions (Welch t 0.18) and negative at 3, 5 and 10. The trigger fires only at the loose thresholds where the lift has already decayed to nothing, and the cell has never once occurred with the fragility dial above 50.

killed.title: Long XLP after a tech-over-staples blowout
killed.reason: The excess over SPY on episodes is zero to negative, so it is beta. Pre-2018 is negative (t=-0.62) and the whole result is 2018 onward; dropping 2020 alone takes the 5-session episode t from 1.21 to 0.25. Today's sub-configuration, with tech still below its 52-week high, has an episode lift of roughly zero at ten sessions.

killed.title: Miners overshooting gold, and biotech snapback
killed.reason: Triaged and dropped before an adversarial pass. GDX versus GLD after a 3pp one-day and 8.7pp five-day divergence: t below 1 at every horizon, both directions. XBI at a bottom-5% 21-day rank inside an intact 63-day picture: declustered N of 9 to 10 with incoherent signs across horizons.
